entry.dc:title: Topsoil (0-5 cm) composition in eight arctic catchments in northern Europe (Finland, Norway and Russia)
entry.dc:creator: Reimann C.
entry.dc:description: Frozen topsoil samples (0-5 cm) were collected during March/April 1994 in eight Arctic catchments in northern Europe (four in Russia, three in Finland, one in Norway), at different distances and in different wind directions from the emissions of the Russian mining, roasting and smelting industry on the Kola Peninsula. Between 14 and 25 sites were sampled in each of the eight catchments ranging in size from 12 to 35 km<sup>2</sup>. Results show that close to the smelters in Monchegorsk and Nikel, topsoil is clearly enriched in Ag, As, Bi, Cd, Co, Cr, Cu, Fe, Ni, Pb, Sb, Se, Te and V. Cu and Ni median contents in topsoils collected close to Monchegorsk are about 600 times higher than in the Finnish catchments. The effect of open-cast mining and waste dumps of alkaline rocks from the nephelinite industry near Kirovsk can be seen in the elevated contents of Al, Ba, K, La, Mn, Na, Sr, Ti, Y and Zn in topsoil collected in a nearby catchment. For many elements, however, variations observed in single catchments are as great as the total regional variation. Several elements (e.g. Cd, Hg, Cu, Ni, Pb, S, Zn) show strong positive correlation between the organic content of the sample and the element content observed. Thus it is necessary to determine the organic content of the samples and correct the element levels when using depth-related soil samples (here, the 0-5 cm topsoil layer) for regional mapping.

entry.dc:title: Cleaning up wismut's waste dumps
entry.dc:creator: Hambeck L.
entry.dc:description: The intensive uranium ore mining activities in Saxony and Thuringia up until 1990 have produced not only some 220,000 t of uranium, but also a multitude of shafts, dumps, sludge ponds, and a big hole left over from open-cast mining, on a total plant area of approx. 37 square kilometers. Decommissioning and disposing of these installations, and cleaning up and recultivating the plant areas, is the purposes and sole activity of Wismut GmbH. Under applicable law, the strategy of the firm is aimed at using modem technical procedures to decommission and dispose of the mining and dressing facilities and make plant areas and the site available for other uses and, in doing so, strike an optimum balance between ecological, economic, and social aspects of cleanup. For this purpose, international experience is utilized by the firm in arranging workshops on important problems. After flooding of the mines and clearing of the tailings had been treated in previous years, a workshop on dump cleanup was organized in Chemnitz in November 1995. The paper deals with aspects of preparing for dump cleanup on the Aue and Ronneburg sites.

entry.dc:title: Trends in open-cast mining
entry.dc:creator: Ruiz Castell A.
entry.dc:description: The mining in open pits of marginal mineralizations with volumes and great deeps is only possible with the introduction of high capacity equipment which requires the use of high technology in the selection of the construction materials as well as of its design. Equally important is the incorporation of the latest advances in data processing which allows an efficient control of the operation and diminishes the time of stops for maintenance and break downs. In this way an important reduction of the extraction costs will be achieved.

entry.dc:title: Mineral economics and occupational health hazards of the asbestos resources of Rajasthan
entry.dc:creator: Mansinghka B.
entry.prism:publicationName: Journal of the Geological Society of India
entry.dc:description: World's largest anthophyllite and tremolite deposits occur as small pods and lenses in the Precambrian ultramafic rocks of South Rajasthan. These deposits are being exploited by small-scale manual, open-cast mining methods. The recovered ore is pulverised, without beneficiation, for use in asbestos-cement products that are manufactured in the small-scale industrial units throughout the country. Field survey conducted for mining, milling, and processing units did not yield anomalous health hazard results. The industry falls under the "extremely low-risk" catergory of the "Notion of acceptable risks". The paper attempts to rationally examine the facts and fallacies associated with asbestos mining and focuses attention on its risk-benefit aspect. It is concluded that the curbs imposed on asbestos are not justified.
entry.authkeywords: Asbestos | Health Hazards | Mineral Economics | Rajasthan

entry.dc:title: Semi-mobile crusher ready for operation in 14 months a challenge for design and manufacture
entry.dc:creator: Baben R.
entry.dc:description: MAN TAKRAF Fordetechnik offers a wide range of equipment and machines in the field of plant engineering, mining and materials handling. In open-cast mining, MTF products are used all over the world for mining and transport of over-burden and minerals. With the supply of the semi-mobile crusher station for Escondida MTF have now expanded their existing range of products to include all necessary equipment for in-pit crushing plants. This article gives an insight into modern crusher technology as well as into advanced engineering techniques practised by MAN TAKRAF - a re-organised and newly formed company with decades of experience.

entry.dc:title: Recultivation in the Lusatian mining region - Targets and prospects
entry.dc:creator: Häge K.
entry.dc:description: For more than 100 years, lignite is mined in open-cast mines in the Lusatian region of northeastern Germany. The increase of output quantities in the former GDR of up to about 200 million tons per year lead to problems for recultivation and loss of public acceptance. By 1993, about 39,000 ha of land were reclaimed, but 75,000 ha of land had been utilized by open-cast mining operations until that date. Forest recultivation has a tradition of more than 60 years and shows the ways for an economically acceptable recultivation by the mining industry. Agricultural recultivation of dumps is also performed successfully. Today, the future mining operation of LAUBAG being reduced to 5 open-cast mines uses specific overburden removal technologies in order to create favourable conditions for the arrangement of a safe, variable and Lusatia-typical post-mining landscape - the beginnings are already visible.
entry.authkeywords: agricultural recultivation | forest recultivation | lignite mining | mine spoils | post mining landscapes | reforestation

entry.dc:title: North Carolina natural phosphate: a geologic and agronomic overview
entry.dc:creator: Gilmore I.
entry.dc:description: PCS Phosphate operates an open-pit phosphate mine in the central coastal plane of North Carolina. Phosphate ore is recovered at the Aurora facility by open-cast mining techniques. This final concentrate is used to manufacture dry and liquid fertilizers at a chemical facility located adjacent to the phosphate ore-processing plant. -from Authors

entry.dc:title: Early-diagenetic deformation structures in the overburden of the bełchatw brown-coal mine (central poland): A predictive tool regarding engineering-geological conditions during exploitation
entry.dc:creator: Van Loon A.J.
entry.dc:description: This chapter focuses on the early-diagenetic deformation structures in the overburden of the belchatów brown-coal mine. Optimization of open-cast mining, including removal of the overburden, requires good planning that should be based on reliable prediction of the working conditions. Investigations made in this framework, in connection with opencast mining of unconsolidated sediments, tend to focus on the characteristics of the sediments with respect to: (1) their workability by mining equipment (excavators, conveyor belts, etc.), (2) the dewatering of the material, and (3) the stability of the mine's slopes. Such analyses are traditionally based on lithology, the vertical succession of layers with different lithology, and the physical mechanical parameters of all lithological units. The choice of the most appropriate system depends on the specific purpose of the investigation and on the geological characteristics of the study area. In the case of the Belchatów mine, the classification should, obviously, be aimed at a system that would be helpful for developing measures to solve (or, if possible, prevent) engineering-geological and mining problems. © 1994, Elsevier Science B.V. All rights reserved.

entry.dc:title: Prediction of groundwater table lowering for lignite open-cast mining in a karstic terrain in western Macedonia, Greece
entry.dc:creator: Kavvadas M.J.
entry.dc:description: Planning for the development of new lignite mines in the Ptolemais basin in western Macedonia, Greece, required the investigation of the hydrogeological characteristics of the adjacent karstic aquifer, since open-cast exploitation involves extensive and sustained groundwater table lowering (up to 260 metres). Review and evaluation of existing hydrological hydrogeological data shows that groundwater flow is to the southeast in a single highly transitive karstified marble aquifer. An analytical regional flow model based on the finite element method is developed and used to assess the feasibility of the required groundwater table lowering and its effects on the hydrological budget of lake Vegoritis, nine kilometres from the mines and in hydraulic continuity with the karstic aquifer. -from Authors

entry.dc:title: The effects of dust on vegetation-a review
entry.dc:creator: Farmer A.M.
entry.dc:description: An increase in quarrying, open-cast mining and road traffic suggest that dust deposition onto vegetation may be increasing. This review describes the physical and chemical characters of a range of dust types. The effects of dust on crops, grasslands, heathlands, trees and woodlands, arctic bryophyte and lichen communities are identified. Dust may affect photosynthesis, respiration, transpiration and allow the penetration of phytotoxic gaseous pollutants. Visible injury symptoms may occur and generally there is decreased productivity. Most of the plant communities are affected by dust deposition so that community structure is altered. Epiphytic lichen and Sphagnum dominated communities are the most sensitive of those studied. However, there have been very few detailed studies on natural and semi-natural systems and some dust types are also very understudied. Recommendations for future research are made in order to overcome this deficiency. © 1992.

entry.dc:title: Image processing for detecting environmental pollution in a coal mining district, Montalban area, Spain
entry.dc:creator: Van Der Meer Mohr H.E.C.
entry.dc:description: Coal has been mined in the Montalban area, Teruel, Spain, since time immemorial. Originally, small-scale surface mining was carried out for domestic purposes. This later developed into commercial underground mining, and after 1983 in open-cast mining using modern excavation techniques which caused serious environmental pollution. In 1991, mining activities stopped almost completely because of economic constraints. At least 3000 miners lost their jobs and the open-cast mines were abandoned. These mines will present a serious problem for future environmental control. Digital image processing of satellite images permits the unique identification of the locations of mining activity and pollution. Moreover, a GIS can be used for environmental monitoring and also for the construction of subsurface structure contour maps, derivative maps such as thickness of overburden, and perspective views. -Authors

entry.dc:title: Influence of mining activities on changes in surface morphology, as exemplified by a brown coal mine at Sieniawa Lubuska
entry.dc:creator: Piotrowska I.
entry.prism:publicationName: Badania Fizjograficzne Nad Polska Zachodnia Seria A Geografia Fizyczna
entry.dc:description: This article focuses attention upon the influence of open-cast mining on the environment. A description is provided of changes which occurred in the test field over the 1980-85 period. The test field comprised an open pit and the inner waste dump of the Sieniawa mine in the Lubuska Platenau. The area became totally remodelled. The soil and biosphere were destroyed. The article also presents new morphologic forms, ie antropogenic ones: the outer waste dump, the inner dump and a terminal hollow. -English summary

entry.dc:title: Petrological-genetic indications of the suitability of coals for obtaining synthetic liquid fuel
entry.dc:creator: Tsikarev D.
entry.dc:description: The main petrological-genetic characteristics and their limiting values for evaluating the suitability of coals for hydrogenation processing into synthetic liquid fuel have been shown. The brown coals obtained by open-cast mining in the Kansk-Achinsk basin have been found to satisfy the suitability requirements.

entry.dc:title: Matching of shovel-dumper at production planning stage. A mathematical approach
entry.dc:creator: Paul P.K.
entry.prism:publicationName: Journal of Mines Metals and Fuels
entry.dc:description: The paper examines the most important aspects of open-cast mining operation, namely, selecting the exact number of loading and hauling units. Based on preliminary easy to understand factors and corresponding data, a mathematical formulation has been proposed to arrive at such an exact number of the units taking into consideration the entire gamut of opencast operations. Suitable corrections and modifications have also been incorporated to suit various working conditions and cater to different production stages throughout the life of a mine.

entry.dc:title: Bearings for planetary gears in large open-cast mining equipment.
entry.dc:creator: Buch S.
entry.dc:description: The growing number of planetary gears in industrial use demonstrates that this design of gearing is a logical answer to demands for high performance, smaller size and lower costs. In the mid 1950s Mannesmann-Demag Lauchhammer commenced development of planetary gear units for large machines used in open cast mining. Some examples are included in this article to show the development of the bearing arrangements during this period. A new bevel/planetary gear unit for a bucket wheel excavator serves to illustrate one of the most modern designs.

entry.dc:title: The discovery of the Brouzils antimony deposit in the Vendee, Massif Armoricain, France: prospection, description of deposit, proposed exploitation
entry.dc:creator: Le Fur Y.
entry.dc:description: The country rocks of the veins are Lower Palaeozoic greywackes and grey to green shales with intervals of volcanic material. The have been deformed during the Early Devonian and Late Devonian/Early Carboniferous (Bretonian), with the formation of N100° to N135° trending folds accompanied by schistosity, and of shears and slides of the same trend. They have also been affected by N-S, E-W and NE-SW extension and fracturing. The Vendee antimony vein field was detected by bedrock Sb geochemistry and electromagnetic survey, followed by trenching and drilling. The veins, including those of Rochetrejoux and Brouzils, occupy tension gashes and shear fractures related to major phases of activity of the South Armorican faults. The vein field developed at the intersection of two fracture systems and includes N-S structures recognised discontinuously over distances of 2-3km, and a main NE-SW bundle dipping NE at 75°-80°. This structure is 6-7m wide and has been recognised over a length of 800m and down to depths of 50-100m. Five richer columns ranging from 30 to 120m long have been distinguished within the bundle. Chalcedonic quartz and stibnite in variable proportions are the main vein-filling minerals, with very minor carbonates, pyrite and arsenopyrite. The geological reserves are estimated at 6000 t of Sb metal, of which 3000 t can be extracted by open-pit mining, in an ore containing 6-7% Sb. The ore can be processed to give excellent commercial concentrate with no impurities or penalising elements. The Gagneraud-BRGM mining project involves open-cast mining of the first 20m at a rate of 100 t Sb per month, protecting the deeper levels. -from English summary

entry.dc:title: Energy requirements of miners engaged in open-pit coal mining
entry.dc:creator: Pichkhadze G.
entry.dc:description: It has been found that according to the value of daily energy consumption the coal miners engaged in open-cast mining should be referred to group III-IV of work intensity. The determining component of daily energy consumption is energy consumption during the working period the value of which depends on the character of working activity and duration of the working shift. The method of strict evaluation of the calorific value of the food taken and the control of body mass is acceptable for the assessment of daily energy consumption.

entry.dc:title: Efficient Extraction of Brown Coal and other Raw Materials using Advanced Surface Mining Technology and Equipment under Different Conditions.
entry.dc:creator: Gerlach P.
entry.dc:description: The GDR covers 72% of its primary energy needs with brown coal. In 1985 it mined 312 Mt of lignite, i. e. 27% of world output. In view of the increasingly worsening conditions of brown coal quality and bedding, more complicated open-cast techniques and equipment is required. The article describes some of the open-cast mining operation under difficult geological conditions.

entry.dc:title: INFLUENCE OF ROCK IMPURITY IN OPEN-CAST MINING ON THE FUSABILITY CHARACTERISTICS OF THE ASH OF THE KANSK-ACHINSK COALS.
entry.dc:creator: Zavorin A.
entry.dc:description: Changes in the chemical composition of the ash due to admixture of the accompanying rocks in the mining of the coals of the Kansk-Achinsk deposit lead to changes in the fusibility of the ash and its viscosity in the molten state. The desirability of limiting the mining contamination with rock to a figure of 2. 5% on the saleable weight of the coal in the dry state is shown.

entry.dc:title: MODERNISING AUSTRIA'S IRON MOUNTAIN MINE.
entry.dc:creator: Anon
entry.dc:description: Steirische Erzberg, the massive 800-m-high iron ore mountain of southern Austria, is the site of one of Europe's largest open-cast mining operations. Considered the most substantial siderite deposit on the continent, and rich also in manganese, it has been the mainstay of Austria's steel industry for seven centuries. The mine has been mechanised so that the operation will be extracting more than 150 million t of rock and iron ore over the next decade. It is estimated that the operation will continue on the present scale until the year 2035.

entry.dc:title: IMPROVING THE LOAD CARRYING CHARACTERISTICS OF UNCOMPACTED FILLS BY PRELOADING.
entry.dc:creator: Charles J.
entry.prism:publicationName: Municipal Engineer Institution of Civil Engineers
entry.dc:description: The load carrying properties of uncompacted fills can be improved by a temporary preloading with a surcharge of fill. Case histories of preloading open-cast mining backfills, old domestic refuse, infilled docks and lagoon pulverized fuel ash are described. The effectiveness of preloading in different situations is discussed and the principles involved in the designing of an adequate surcharge are outlined.

entry.dc:title: Wear in lignite open-cast mining work.
entry.dc:creator: Schwein B.
entry.dc:description: Excavators, dumpers and belt conveyor plants suffer wear in lignite open-cast mining, but excavator shovel cutting edges, etc. can be protected in this connection. Hard facing, shaped castings with incorporated carbides, checking and control of surface pressures, friction and kinematic conditions, reduction of the number of wear points, and rationalization of repair work are advantageous. The future increase from 1:2,5 to 1:6 in the coal/waste ratio will further intensify problems in this connection.

entry.dc:title: DISCUSSION ON THE TESTING OF CUTTING RESISTANCE AND TRUCK PERFORMANCE.
entry.dc:creator: Liu J.
entry.dc:description: This paper concentrates on testing the cutting resistance of rocks and coal and testing truck performance. It is an important means for conducting planning, production and research in selecting optimal open-cast mining technology and transportation equipment. Examples are given to illustrate mining and technical parameters, and curves show the relations obtained. On the site tests can be used as criteria for planning optimal mining technology, and the selection, introduction and use of equipment by taking into account geological conditions of Chinese coal fields.

entry.dc:title: Occurrence and use of secondary raw materials in czechoslovakian industry during 1982
entry.dc:creator: Vojta M.
entry.prism:publicationName: Statistical Journal of the United Nations Economic Commission for Europe
entry.dc:description: The growing quantities of waste materials from production and consumption of industrial commodities receive special attention by Czechoslovakian authorities. A statistical survey was undertaken in 1982, which provided data on the quantities of industrial wastes generated in production as well as on the extent to which such wastes were recycled. Mineral wastes account for more than 90 per cent of total solid wastes, and overburden from lignite open-cast mining is by far its most significant component. Recycling remains at present unsatisfactory particularly for this category of waste. By contrast, recycling of metal scraps is practiced widely. Future improvement in recycling is expected from current experiments with a recycling register. © 1985 IOS Press. All rights Reserved.
